CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

Backported the upstream Storable SX_HOOK I32_MAX guard from Perl commit e4f681784bcdeaa91ff02a2fa4cdcae5c46779d7 into the DHI perl package. The patched package rejects an SX_HOOK item count of I32_MAX before calling av_extend, so the signed overflow panic during thaw/retrieve is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream S_measure_struct overflow guards from Perl commits 5f7eb6bbbe0510964e3fb1d6bb691e5445913e55 and 40754edc72dd3e513d758153c0e2f0215897740e into the DHI perl package. The patched package croaks when a pack/unpack structure size would overflow SSize_t and uses overflow-safe bit/nibble length math, so the out-of-bounds heap read is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream Perl_study_chunk trie overflow guard from Perl commit 03f74bbbd3a68350d926ee93d56ee4808c28c4c7 into the DHI perl package. The patched package skips trie optimization when the start-to-tail delta would overflow a 16-bit field, so the silently incorrect match behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream HTTP::Tiny 0.095 credentialed-redirect hardening (allow_credentialed_redirects / allow_downgrade defaults, plus protocol-relative Location handling) into the bundled HTTP::Tiny shipped by the DHI perl package. The patched HTTP::Tiny strips caller-supplied Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization headers on cross-origin redirects and refuses https-to-http redirects by default, so the credential-forwarding behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream HTTP::Tiny CRLF / control-character validation fix (release-0.093, commit d73c7651e82ace02693842df55928b6c3ae7c38d) into the bundled HTTP::Tiny shipped by the DHI perl package. The patched HTTP::Tiny rejects CR, LF, and other control characters in the request method, Request-URI, the URL-derived Host header, and HTTP/1.1 control-field header values before they are written to the socket, so the header-injection / request-smuggling behavior is mitigated inline.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress IO::Uncompress::Unzip _dosToUnixTime hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched _dosToUnixTime short-circuits to 0 for a zero DOS datetime and wraps Time::Local::timelocal() in an eval guard so out-of-range month/day/hour values no longer raise an uncaught exception out of IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($file), so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress zipdetails hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched zipdetails CLI calls the correctly spelled unpackValue_Q helper when decoding 8-byte UID/GID values from Info-ZIP Unix Extra Fields (closing the published undefined-subroutine crash), and decode_ux now validates the UID/GID Size byte through canDecodeLittleEndian and reports invalid or zero sizes as bad data instead of triggering internalFatal, so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.
Backported the upstream IO::Compress Unzip fix into the DHI perl package. The patched package fixes a typo in the fastForward method, so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.
